plain.text: The LORD said to Abram, "Leave your country, your relatives and your father's household, and go to the land I will show you. I will make you into a great nation and bless you; I will make your name great, and you will be a blessing. I will bless those who bless you and curse those who curse you, and all the families of the earth will be blessed through you." So Abram went, as the LORD had told him, at seventy-five years old, with Sarai, Lot and all they had. They came to Canaan. The LORD appeared to Abram and said, "To your offspring I will give this land." Abram built altars to the LORD there and called on his name.

There was a famine, so Abram went down to Egypt. Because Sarai was beautiful, he was afraid the Egyptians would kill him to take her, so he told her to say she was his sister. Pharaoh's officials praised her to Pharaoh, and she was taken into his palace. Pharaoh treated Abram well for her sake. But the LORD struck Pharaoh's household with serious diseases. Pharaoh summoned Abram: "What have you done to me? Why didn't you tell me she was your wife?" He gave her back and sent them away with all they had.

summary.bigIdea: God calls Abram to leave home and promises to bless him and, through him, all the families of the earth.
points: God calls Abram to go to an unknown land.
God promises: "All the families of the earth will be blessed through you."
Abram obeys, but then lies out of fear in Egypt, and God protects Sarai.
summary.reflection: Abram went without knowing where he was going. Is God asking you to take a step of trust?
